key_insight: MUSE maps glioma MRI heterogeneity by physical distance and direction, showing substantial overlap with directional radiomics rather than evidence of drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: This research may support imaging-based characterization of glioma, but it does not establish clinical utility or guide treatment selection.
method: Analyzed postcontrast T1-weighted MRI and enhancing-tumor segmentations from 416 UCSF-PDGM patients.
Compared native 3D MUSE variograms with directional GLCM radiomics in 375 paired cases.
Tested IDH associations using patient-level permutations and evaluated a separate 3D CNN for IDH classification.
evidence_signal: MUSE and half GLCM contrast correlated strongly across 9,371 aligned offsets (r = 0.954); the independent CNN achieved out-of-fold IDH ROC-AUC 0.792 and PR-AUC 0.414.
watch_item: In grade-4 tumors, the MUSE–IDH association weakened after directional GLCM adjustment (p = 0.256), limiting evidence of added molecular information beyond those radiomic features.
paper_title: Multiscale Spatial Characterization of Glioma MRI with MUSE and Radiomics
